Compare with this passage what is said about the ὑπτίαις χερσὶ [upturned hands] of suppliants in Thes. vol. 8 p. 493.

Thus Karsten for ἄξειν νιν [to lead him] (ἄξει νιν [he will lead him] Triclinius). ὑπτίασμα [a supine position] is used improperly of Orestes, the avenger of his father's murder, whose return would be, as it were, a raising up of the prostrate Agamemnon: see Karsten's note p. 275. Yet strangely in this sense ὑπτίασμα [a supine position] is used, which seems to signify rather a casting down than a raising up, like ὑπτιασμός [a supine position], a wrestling term, about which Jacobs spoke on Philostr.
